\section[śubhāśayagaḷu]{\kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು} (śubhāśayagaḷu) — best wishes}

\label{lesson:KA-C105-wishes}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a driver, then the Kannada for a shop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು}} (\emph{śubhāśayagaḷu}) — \textquotedblleft{}best wishes\textquotedblright{}, \textbf{\kn{ಶುಭ}} (\emph{śubha}), \textquotedblleft{}good\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ಆಶಯ}} (\emph{āśaya}), \textquotedblleft{}wish\textquotedblright{}, in the plural.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Good wishes, many of them.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śubhāśayagaḷu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śubhāśayagaḷu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{śubhāśayagaḷu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a driver, then the Kannada for a shop, then say \emph{śubhāśayagaḷu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Best wishes\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[habba]{\kn{ಹಬ್ಬ} (habba) — festival}

\label{lesson:KA-C105-festival}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a shop, then the Kannada for best wishes.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹಬ್ಬ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಬ್ಬ}} (\emph{habba}) — \textquotedblleft{}festival\textquotedblright{}, the second half of \textbf{\kn{ಹುಟ್ಟುಹಬ್ಬ}}, \textquotedblleft{}birthday\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಹಬ್ಬದ} \kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು}} (\emph{habbada śubhāśayagaḷu}) — \textquotedblleft{}festival greetings\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The festival inside birthday.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{habba}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a shop, then the Kannada for best wishes, then say \emph{habba} again

\textbf{\kn{ಆತಿಥ್ಯ}} (\emph{ātithya}) — \textquotedblleft{}hospitality\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\kn{ಅತಿಥಿ}} (\emph{atithi}), \textquotedblleft{}guest\textquotedblright{}.

What a guest thanks the host for.
\end{grammarlens}
